articles.title: Diving deeper into Cavs narrow 125-121 victory over the Nets
articles.summary: The Cavs are a work in progress.
articles.body:
CLEVELAND — The Cleveland Cavaliers nearly fumbled a 22-point fourth-quarter lead as they defeated the Brooklyn Nets 125-121 in their home opener.

28 points, 9 rebounds, 1 assist, 4 steals

Being an off-ball scoring threat on an otherwise inept offense is difficult. Ideally, Porter would be creating looks through his movement and receiving passes from someone that actually requires defensive attention — say, Nikola Jokic. Instead, Porter has to work off Egor Demin and Julius Randle, which isn't always the easiest task.

However, Porter made that look easy this game. He was disruptive off-ball, drawing the defense's attention away from the play, and when he did get an opening, he made the most of it. This was on top of being an impactful defender.

Allen was limited to 27 minutes, presumably because of the knee injury he is playing through , but made the most of his time on the court. He was aggressive attacking in the pick-and-roll when the Nets blitzed the ball handler, and even threw in a three-point make from the top of the arc.

Aside from maybe the three-point attempt, this was exactly what you want to see from Allen. And the Cavs were once again better off because he was a meaningful part of the offensive attack.

22 points, 4 assists, 5 rebounds, 1 steal

Mitchell's scoring is in midseason form. There are things you could criticize him for in these first two games— particularly the turnovers — but scoring isn't one of them.

The shotmaking has felt effortless at the start of the season. He's doing a good job of creating space off the dribble, allowing him to score at all three levels. Interestingly enough, Mitchell isn't hunting off-the-dribble threes as much as we've seen in the past. He's only taken 10 triples through two games, with most of them being catch-and-shoot threes. The three-point volume is something to keep an eye on as the season progresses.

7 points, 1 assist, 8 rebounds, 2 turnovers, 6 fouls

This was a tough game for Sharpe. Defensively, he struggled to contain Allen and Evan Mobley — who had a good game in his own right — and fouled James Harden twice on three-point attempts. This all led to him fouling out midway through the fourth quarter.

Offensively, he struggled to make much of an impact against Cleveland's bigs. He went just 3-for-10 from the field while turning it over three times.

Tyson provided a solid contribution off the bench. He played with energy, knocked down some threes, and did a good job finding open teammates as a connector. This was basically an ideal game for him.

Assists like this show why Harden is one of the best passers in NBA history. Few guards would've seen this angle, let alone been able to fit the ball into such a tight window.

This was a bright spot in what was an overall a poor showing from Harden.

"This is a building block. It's time spent. It's adversity. I think Joe Mazzulla said something like everybody loves each other in training camp. But you understand, like hey, come December, come January, and we're missing shots…who are we then? That all comes in the regular season." – Donovan Mitchell on the early season struggles

"This is a building block. It's time spent. It's adversity. I think Joe Mazzulla said something like everybody loves each other in training camp. But you understand, like hey, come December, come January, and we're missing shots…who are we then? That all comes in the regular season."

– Donovan Mitchell on the early season struggles

The Cavs have been outscored 73-45 combined in the fourth quarter through two games.

Late game execution has left a lot to be desired.

This game will be remembered for the Cavaliers not learning their lesson from Thursday

The Cavs didn't give up their 22-point fourth-quarter lead, but it didn't stop them from trying. The Nets cut the deficit down to two by winning the fourth quarter in the closing minute before the Cavs iced the game at the free-throw line. Brooklyn won the final frame 41-29.

The Cavaliers spent the time since Thursday's loss to the Sixers talking about how they need to do a better job of handling leads . They didn't do that here. If they were playing a team that was slightly more competent than the Nets, they likely would've dropped this one as well.

The Cavs are clearly a work in progress. They're incorporating new pieces into the rotation that will take some time. However, it's impossible to feel great about what you've seen so far — particularly in their first two fourth quarters.

articles.title: SEC college football playoff outlook: Dissecting logjam of 2-loss teams in contested league
articles.summary: The SEC now has seven two-loss teams that are still in contention for the College Football Playoff.
articles.body:
If you're looking for some clarity on which teams are legitimate College Football Playoff threats inside the SEC, Week 8 made a mess of things. After Saturday, we now have multiple two-loss teams inside the conference that will be a mess to sort out.

On Saturday, No. 11 Tennessee suffered its second loss of the season to South Carolina on the road, and No. 4 Ole Miss lost 34-27 in a thriller to No. 19 Texas in Austin. No. 18 LSU improved to 6-2 with a 38-17 win over Auburn on the road, and No. 13 Alabama got a victory over Texas A&M, 31-20.

There are also two-loss teams in the SEC in Missouri, Florida and Georgia, which all had byes this week.

Here's an attempt at sorting out the logjam that is the SEC, which has multiple two-loss teams that appear to be in the hunt for the College Football Playoff after Week 8.

Ole Miss got its first signature win with a 32-24 victory over then-No. 7 LSU in Week 3. The Rebels also have ranked wins over Louisville and a 31-3 win over then-No. 13 Missouri last week.

Ole Miss' first loss came on the road against Florida, but the Gators were ranked No. 21 at the time and are back in the rankings after a win over Texas on the road last week. Ole Miss also defeated Vanderbilt on the road, 52-17.

Against Texas, the Rebels did come back from a 24-3 deficit at halftime and tied the game early in the fourth quarter. The Rebels even responded after going down 10 late, scoring a field goal with 1:22 left, and a recovered onside kick gave Trinidad Chambliss a chance at a Hail Mary that Texas held off. The committee won't fault Ole Miss for losing on the road too much, but the Rebels can't afford to stumble.

Ole Miss has just one ranked team remaining on its schedule, as it is set to play No. 5 Georgia on Nov. 7. Elsewhere in the SEC, Ole Miss draws Auburn and Mississippi State at home and goes on the road to play Oklahoma on Nov. 14. If the Rebels win out, a CFP bid is likely. Three losses, even against a very good team in Georgia, make it seem unlikely.

Alabama has a strong resume, with road wins over Kentucky and Mississippi State. The Tide also have conference wins over South Carolina and Texas A&M, including a 48-10 Week 1 win over East Carolina.

As for the losses, Alabama lost to No. 2 Georgia on a last-second field goal and fell 26-10 on the road to Tennessee last week. The committee likely won't fault the Tide for either of their losses. But Alabama cannot afford to lose to any of its remaining opponents: LSU in Baton Rouge on Nov. 7, Vanderbilt, Chattanooga or Auburn at home for the Iron Bowl.

If the Tide win on the road against LSU, it would almost guarantee a bid, assuming they win out.

LSU beat Clemson 58-10 in Week 1, and although Dabo Swinney's team wasn't ranked, the committee will value a big nonconference win like that. LSU also beat Louisiana Tech and McNeese State outside of the SEC.

As for the Tigers' conference wins, they have some solid ones, such as a 35-6 win over Texas A&M when the Aggies were ranked at the time and a win over then-No. 16 Mississippi State. On Saturday, LSU went on the road and beat Auburn, which just beat Georgia last week, 38-17.

LSU's losses don't look terrible. The first was on the road to Ole Miss, which the Tigers had a chance to beat late. The other was also on the road, against Kentucky, which looks like one of the best surprise teams in the SEC.

The Tigers have a tough remaining slate, featuring three straight ranked opponents: Alabama and Texas at home on Nov. 7 and 8, respectively, and a road trip to Tennessee on Nov. 21. LSU closes out the season against 3-4 Arkansas on the road.

Texas' CFP resume is a mess, to say the least. The Longhorns' best win came in Week 2, with a come-from-behind win over then-No. 1 Ohio State. Texas also defeated then-No. 14 Tennessee on the road 20-17, including non-conference wins over Texas State and UTSA.

The Longhorns' two losses are puzzling, both to unranked teams in Oklahoma and Florida at home. Texas' Arch Manning threw two interceptions against a struggling Sooners team. The next week, Texas lost at home to an unranked Florida which had lost back-to-back games to Missouri and South Carolina.

But with a huge 34-27 home win over a very good Ole Miss team, the Longhorns are still alive. Texas has remaining home conference games against unranked Mississippi State and Arkansas, and goes on the road to play No. 22 Missouri and No. 18 LSU next month. The Longhorns will end the regular season on the road against Texas A&M. While Texas would be in with two losses, the win over Ohio State earlier in the season might give Texas a case with three losses, depending on how the Buckeyes finish

Tennessee's case took a hit on Saturday, as the Vols were upset 27-24 on the road against unranked South Carolina on Saturday. The Vols' only other loss came at home, a close 20-17 one to Texas in a game that Tennessee was very much in.

The Vols' biggest signature win came two weeks ago, beating then-No. 6 Alabama 26-10 at home. Tennessee also has wins over Georgia Tech and Arkansas on the road, as well as a conference win over Auburn.

The Vols have two ranked teams still to play, including at home vs. No. 7 Kentucky next week, and a home game against LSU on Nov. 21. Tennessee also plays at Texas A&M and Vanderbilt, but the Vols should be heavy favorites in both those games. MORE: How bad Week 8 losses by Texas Tech, BYU impact Big 12's CFP outlook

The Florida Gators are the most confusing team in the entire SEC. Florida burst into the CFP picture with its dominant 52-38 win over then-No. 4 Ole Miss at home in Week 4. The Gators then dropped back-to-back games on the road to Missouri and lost to a three-loss, unranked South Carolina team at home.

The Gators then went on the road last week and upset Texas, winning 27-24. Just how good this Florida team is will come down to how it does the rest of the season. The Gators biggest test is next week, taking on No. 5 Georgia in Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Ga.

Florida also has to go on the road to play Kentucky on Nov. 14. Florida then has remaining home conference games against Oklahoma and Vanderbilt, and plays rival Florida State on the road to close out the regular season.

Missouri might be the team least likely to make the field, thanks to what it's done so far and what it still has in front of it. The Tigers beat non-conference Kansas 38-21 in Week 2, and took down then-No. 8 Florida at home on Oct. 3.

The Tigers also beat Texas A&M 27-6 at home, with losses to ranked conference opponents in Mississippi State and Ole Miss.

Missouri has a brutal stretch next month, featuring games against No. 19 Texas, at No. 5 Georgia and vs. No. 12 Kentucky at home before a regular-season home finale against Oklahoma. However unlikely, the Tigers will likely be in the hunt if it makes it out of that stretch undefeated.

College Football Playoffs odds for SEC teams

(Odds listed via DraftKings after Ole Miss lost to Texas)

How many SEC teams have gotten into CFP each year

A look at the previous two 12-team fields:

No. 5 Texas, No. 9 Tennessee, No. 2 Georgia

No. 7 Texas A&M, No. 3 Georgia No. 6 Ole Miss No. 8 Oklahoma, No. 9 Alabama

Last season was the one year in which the expanded CFP had a bit of controversy. The committee gave a bid to three-loss Alabama, despite the Tide getting pummeled by Georgia 28-7 in the SEC title game. The committee opted to give the Tide a bid to reward them for making a conference title game. As a result, two-loss Notre Dame, which is independent and thus did not play in a conference title game, did not get a bid.

All other teams listed had just two losses and still made the field.

Of course, the CFP field usually works itself out, and the SEC will likely be a bloodbath over the next few weeks. But depending on how things shake out, it could be quite interesting for the committee to try to determine which two-loss SEC teams are worthy of bids.

articles.title: No. 25 Wildcats claw Cyclones
articles.summary: Connor Moberly replaces Raynor in second half at quarterback
articles.body:
TUCSON, Ariz. — Quarterbacks Jaylen Raynor and Connor Moberly combined for 169 passing yards, but Iowa State struggled to maintain offensive traction on the ground in a 39-3 loss to Arizona on Saturday at Casino Del Sol Stadium.

The Cyclones (3-4, 1-3) were limited to 221 total yards of offense and 14 first downs while being kept out of the end zone throughout the contest. Arizona (6-1, 3-1) controlled the tempo with 477 total yards, led by quarterback Noah Fifita, who completed 27 of 34 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns.

Arizona set an aggressive tone early, taking an 8-0 lead just 31 seconds into the game when Fifita connected with Isaiah Mizell on a 71-yard touchdown pass, followed by a two-point conversion pass to Tyler Powell. The Wildcats expanded their lead to 15-0 later in the opening quarter on a 6-yard touchdown run by Quincy Craig. Iowa State answered with its most effective drive of the quarter, marching 53 yards in seven plays. The possession was sparked by a 32-yard completion from Raynor to tight end Vince Benetti down to the Arizona 14-yard line. After Raynor was sacked for a 10-yard loss by Malcolm Hartzog and Dominic Lolesio, Kyle Konrardy got the Cyclones on the board with a 40-yard field goal with 1:06 remaining in the first quarter.

The Cyclones engineered another promising drive early in the second quarter, driving 55 yards in eight plays to reach the Arizona 20-yard line. Raynor jump-started the advance with a 17-yard pass to Omari Hayes and a 27-yard completion to Jamal Polite, advancing the ball to the Wildcats' 29-yard line. Raynor then connected with Easton Miller for 5 yards to setup third-and-short, but after a 2-yard pass to Ty Claiborne on fourth down fell short of the line to gain, Iowa State turned the ball over on downs at the 20. Arizona capitalized with a 15-play, 80-yard drive capped by Kedrick Reescano's 5-yard touchdown run. In the final two minutes of the half, Raynor completed passes of 8 yards to Claiborne and 12 yards to Cody Jackson, aided by a 15-yard pass interference penalty on Dwight Bootle II. However, Raynor fumbled on a scramble at the Arizona 49-yard line, recovered by Tyrese Boss. Arizona's Michael Salgado-Medina missed a 31-yard field goal attempt as time expired in the half with Arizona leading 25-3.

Defensive execution dominated the third quarter, which ended completely scoreless. Moberly opened the half under center for Iowa State, completing a 12-yard pass to Hayes and later connecting with Miller for an 18-yard gain to cross midfield. Cornerback Keyon Washington delivered a highlight for the Cyclone defense by forcing a fumble on Arizona's Caleb Smith, which bounced out of bounds. A 5-yard penalty on Iowa State for running into the kicker on a fake punt extended an Arizona drive, but the Cyclones held firm to force a Chase Ridley punt.

Iowa State opened the final quarter with a 13-play, 36-yard drive highlighted by an 8-yard rush from Aiden Flora and a 6-yard scramble by Moberly. After a punt, the Cyclones regained possession down 32-3 following a 40-yard touchdown pass from Fifita to Henry Gabalis. Moberly ripped off a 12-yard run to the ISU 37 and completed a 5-yard pass to Benetti. However, back-to-back incompletions and a 7-yard sack by Dash Fifita ended the possession on downs at the Iowa State 36-yard line. Arizona backup quarterback Sawyer Anderson concluded the scoring with a 4-yard touchdown run with 1:55 remaining. Iowa State's final drive featured a 6-yard rush by Ryver Peppers before Nela Taliauli recorded a 4-yard sack to force a final punt.

Raynor completed 8 of 10 passes for 106 yards, while Moberly went 7 for 17 for 63 yards through the air and added 35 gross rushing yards (20 net). Flora paced the Cyclone rushing attack with 36 yards on 12 carries. Benetti finished as Iowa State's leading receiver with three catches for 42 yards, while Hayes added two receptions for 29 yards, Polite caught one pass for 27 yards and Miller recorded two catches for 23 yards.

Linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen anchored the Iowa State defense with a game high 15 total tackles, including a sack and two tackles for loss. Carson Willich recorded 10 tackles.

articles.title: ‘What a disgusting disgusting offense’: Dave Portnoy tells Michigan coach to ‘go get a plane ticket to the moon’ after loss
articles.summary: The Michigan Wolverines suffered a disappointing loss to the Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday, despite several chances to put the visitors away. The Wolverines’...
articles.body:
The Michigan Wolverines suffered a disappointing loss to the Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday, despite several chances to put the visitors away. The Wolverines' defense came to play, holding the No. 6-ranked team to 13 points in an overtime loss; instead, their offense and its coordinator may be to blame.

Michigan lost 13-6 after a disappointing overtime battle, and fans and critics are beyond disappointed with the "disgusting" display of football the Wolverines have shown recently.

Barstool founder and notorious Wolverines fan Dave Portnoy immediately took to social media to rip Michigan's offensive coordinator, Jason Beck, saying he felt the team's loss was ultimately on him.

"They're too talented on offense to be this pathetic," Portnoy said via X . "It doesn't matter; I think Bryce Underwood probably gives us the best chance to win, and he was a scapegoat. Bryce Underwood was a scapegoat for Jason Beck.

"Jason Beck is horrific. Jason Beck is the worst offensive play caller, worst offensive coordinator I've ever watched with these eyes. Jason Beck, get him out. If you want to, just make him the water boy. Take the play calling away from Jason Beck; Jason Beck doesn't know what the f*** he's doing. Jason Beck is disgusting."

Portnoy didn't blame the players; instead, he blamed the coaches. Michigan started freshman quarterback Tommy Carr over Bryce Underwood, and the Wolverines struggled in the red zone on Saturday. Facing third-and-1 from the Indiana 1-yard line, Beck called a naked bootleg, and Carr was sacked for a 13-yard loss. The drive was then squandered on a missed field goal by kicker Trey Butkowski. Although the sack and the miss were blown plays by two specific players, the play calling from Beck leading up to those moments is something fans like Portnoy can't comprehend.

"They played hard, Michigan, but what a disgusting, disgusting offense and disgusting, disgusting game to watch. Defense plays their nuts off; defense deserves a win. But Jason Beck, go get a plane ticket to the f***ing moon and let's shoot you there."

During a postgame press conference, head coach Kyle Whittingham shielded Beck from media bullets while taking accountability for the poor play calling.

"Everything falls on my shoulders, so whatever happens in the course of a game is on me," Whittingham said, via Sports Illustrated . "That was not a good football call, no, that was not a good call at that point in time.

"I have the ability to overrule anything in the whole program. And so, like I said, it circles back to me, but it was a very disappointing outcome and a call that I know Jason wishes he had back, because it really was damaging."

Next weekend, Michigan will travel to New Jersey to face the Rutgers Scarlet Knights, hoping to redeem their season.

articles.title: Aaron Ashby approaches history with latest dominant performance for Brewers
articles.summary: The lefty reliever has been the Brewers' best pitcher this postseason.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are now two wins away from their first World Series title, thanks to an unlikely hero.

Lefty reliever Aaron Ashby has been a reliable reliever in the past three seasons, but he has completely dominated the competition this postseason. Ashby has been the Brewers' best reliever, over closer Trevor Megill, and it showed in Milwaukee's Game 2 win on Saturday night.

Manager Pat Murphy trusted Ashby to get the final five outs in a 5-4 win over the Tampa Bay Rays instead of turning to Megill. That remained the case even when Ashby allowed a leadoff double in the ninth inning, and even when the dangerous Yandy Diaz was at the plate.

Ashby's performance has not only put the Brewers up 2-0, but it has also put his name on an exclusive list of playoff performers. Here's a look at the history Ashby is making this October.

In eight Ashby appearances, Pat Murphy has now asked the lefty to get at least five outs seven times, and Ashby has now closed the game with a save three times in the playoffs.

After throwing 1.2 scoreless innings in Game 2 on Saturday night, Ashby has now thrown 15.2 innings of scoreless baseball in the postseason. That puts him one out away from Andrew Miller's all-time record of 16 scoreless innings to begin a postseason, which Miller set with Cleveland in 2016.

Like Miller, Ashby is being used for multiple innings and against the opposing teams' best hitters, regardless of whether they are lefties or righties. Ashby is a former starter, just like Miller, so he isn't a stranger to giving the Brewers multiple innings.

Miller ultimately let up three runs in his final two playoff appearances during that 2016 playoff run. Therefore, if Ashby doesn't allow a run the rest of the way, he will hold the record for most innings in a single playoff run without letting up a run.

articles.title: Kochetkov Earns Shutout – Hurricanes 4, Blues 0
articles.summary: Pyotr Kochetkov improved his record to 7-0-0 with a 24 save shutout and the Carolina Hurricanes defeated the St. Louis Blues on Saturday night, 4-0. The Hurr...
articles.body:
Pyotr Kochetkov improved his record to 7-0-0 with a 24 save shutout and the Carolina Hurricanes defeated the St. Louis Blues on Saturday night, 4-0. The Hurricanes now have a 9-2-2 record and their 20 points put them at first place in the league, (for now).

The Canes finished up their road trip with a 3-1-1 record and will return home for their next game Tuesday night.

After a scoreless first period, the visiting team broke through for three goals in the second.

Sean Walker got the party started four minutes and change into the period off of another sterling assist by Jackson Blake. Just 20 seconds later, Jordan Martinook found Jesperi Kotkaniemi and "KK" made no mistake to put his team up, 2-0.

Speaking of Kotkaniemi, he also had a team high 63% faceoff percentage, (10 of 16). His goal was the third of the season for him. He has been playing better and better since having more of a chance.

Kochetkov now has 12 shutouts in his career.

Later in the second period, Seth Jarvis found Logan Stankoven on a breakaway and Stankoven buried his 8th of the season.

In the third period, Carolina finished off the scoring when Nikolaj Ehlers knocked in a powerplay goal. It was the only powerplay chance of the night for the Hurricanes. They successfully killed the only opportunity that the Blues had with the advantage.

The Canes outshot the Blues in every period and finished up with 39-24 advantage.

The Hurricanes will take Sunday off before returning to practice on Monday.

articles.title: Sharks Locker Room: San Jose Had Winning Road Trip, But It Didn’t Feel That Way Tonight
articles.summary: BOSTON — The San Jose Sharks echoed the same theme, after a 6-4 loss to the Boston Bruins. “Be better […]
articles.body:
BOSTON — The San Jose Sharks echoed the same theme, after a 6-4 loss to the Boston Bruins.

"Be better in front of the net," Will Smith said of four of the Bruins goals, which happened right in front of goalie Alex Nedeljkovic . "They're very preventable."

Smith wasn't a pointing a finger at just his defensemen, but at the whole team, including himself.

Michael Misa , Kiefer Sherwood , Dmitry Orlov , and Smith scored in the back-and-forth tilt.

In the end, the Sharks came out of a six-game road trip with a 3-2-1 record, but it feels like it could've been more, after a 3-1 third period lead at Detroit turned into an OT loss and tonight's 3-2 third period edge ended in a regulation defeat.

After the game, Smith praised Jeremy Swayman's play, Nedeljkovic shared the key on how the San Jose Sharks can defend harder, Orlov discussed the expectations for this team, and Warsofsky summarized where the squad is at 12 games into the season.

A deeper game story with micro-stats from Stathletes and game action clips, Sharks Insight, will be published soon.

Smith, on Swayman's save on him, Bruins up 5-4 late in 3rd: "I think I honestly had that one. It was a quick pump fake and backhander. He made a hell of a save, so we got to tip your cap. He's a hell of a goalie and he played good tonight." — Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) October 25, 2026

Smith, on Swayman's save on him, Bruins up 5-4 late in 3rd: "I think I honestly had that one. It was a quick pump fake and backhander. He made a hell of a save, so we got to tip your cap. He's a hell of a goalie and he played good tonight."

Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) October 25, 2026

Nedeljkovic, on all the net front goals that Boston scored:

I think that's where they scored all their goals except for the Pasta one. All that is, just outwilling guys and wanting to defend harder than the other team wants to score. All it comes down to, no X's and O's, and we had bodies in the area, I think, on all of them, it's just outwilling them a little bit more, just being a little harder on our sticks. I can do a better job, maybe swallowing up another puck or two there and killing plays or putting rebounds in better spots as well.

Orlov: "On paper, everybody expects us to be a good team. But right now, we have to prove it. Not just be a good team on paper. We have to show up every game and battle." — Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) October 25, 2026

Orlov: "On paper, everybody expects us to be a good team. But right now, we have to prove it. Not just be a good team on paper. We have to show up every game and battle."

Orlov, on the San Jose Sharks losing net front battles:

We just shoot ourselves in the foot again. It kind of happens almost every game. We [don't] battle, [don't] win the battles when we have to. We not playing more hungry, for the battles, for the puck, and lost focus sometimes. It's why we give up some goals.

Warsofsky, on the Michael Misa pass to Ty Dellandrea that led to the David Pastrnak goal:

We make a play on the entry, where we got to be smarter than that. We try to make a cross-ice pass with four seconds left in the power play. Pastrnak comes out of the box, he scores. So we got to be smarter.

We got some results. We still have a long way to go. We're still good. Some things we got to get better at. Starts with protecting our net front. That's going to be one. We got to start scoring 5-on-5. That's going to be another one.

We definitely left some points on the table. That's for sure. And we've also gotten points that we probably shouldn't have. So, you know, our record says what it is. It is what it is. If we're going to be a really good hockey team in this league, we got to play a lot better going forward.

Warsofsky, on where the San Jose Sharks are after 12 games this season:

As a coach of the team, we're pushing this team, challenging this team to be better. I thought we'd be a little bit more consistent. I would say that maybe is the biggest thing.

Just his pace. He was holding on to pucks. I thought he was good on the walls and battles. So we'll have to look at some stuff, but I thought he was better.

articles.title: Brewers erase four-run deficit, take 2-0 World Series lead
articles.body:
The 2026 Milwaukee Brewers might have to borrow a 40-year-old slogan from the Goonies: "Never Say Die."

Tonight, the Brewers were facing Drew Rasmussen, the Tampa Bay ace and the best starting pitcher of the postseason so far. Logan Henderson, who hasn't been at his best this postseason, suffered through a disastrous first inning. But if there was one thing that the Brewers proved against the Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, it was that no lead is safe, and this remarkable team will not ever give up. In the parlance of one of the Brewer standouts this evening, the Brewers dragged Rasmussen. The ground out at-bats. They chipped away. Peck, peck, peck. And before it was over, Milwaukee had a couple of new offensive heroes, another huge comeback win, and a 2-0 series lead.

But before all that, it was a nightmare start for the Brewers.

The first batter of the game, Yandy Díaz, worked for seven pitches. The last one, a changeup way below the zone, was hit weakly to shortstop. Cooper Pratt fielded it but rushed the throw, which got by Jake Bauers and into the dugout, putting Díaz at second base. An ominous omen.

Henderson recovered momentarily and struck out Jonathan Aranda for the first out. But Chandler Simpson did Chandler Simpson things, knocking an RBI single into center field, after which he stole second and then scored when Junior Caminero followed with another RBI single. The Rays weren't finished, though: Liam Hicks got an 0-1 cutter right down the middle and hit it out to right center, the first homer of the series, which made it 4-0 Rays with only one out on the board.

Henderson did retire the next two, but the Brewers would have to dig themselves out of a deep hole on this night. Fortunately, they're a team that has proved time and time again that they're a team that brought their shovels to the postseason. They got to work on Rasmussen immediately in the bottom of the first: Jackson Chourio singled, moved to third on a single by Bauers, and then scored when, after a Christian Yelich strikeout, William Contreras came through as he has so many times over the past month with an RBI single through the right side of the infield.

Brice Turang hit into a hard-luck second out when he hit a 109 mph line drive right at Richie Palacios. But Garrett Mitchell kept the pressure on the Rays, and hit a 112 mph single into right that scored Bauers. Pratt struck out to end the inning, but Milwaukee had immediately halved the Rays lead.

A leadoff walk to Victor Mesa Jr. in the second had Henderson on the precipice, but he showed some fight; Taylor Walls bunted, Mesa Jr. over to second but made the first out, and Henderson struck out Díaz and Aranda to get through the inning unscathed. Rasmussen was on his way to a quick inning in the bottom of the second, but Chourio took a hammer to his pitch count when, with two outs, he battled for 11 pitches before hitting a 105 mph groundout. It was a 1-2-3 inning for the Tampa Bay ace, but he had to work hard for it.

Henderson got one more inning and made the most of it, retiring Simpson, Caminero, and Hicks in order. The Brewers were unable to score in the bottom of the inning despite Contreras's second hit of the game (which pushed his batting average in the postseason over .400). In the top of the fourth, JoJo Romero replaced Henderson and worked around a one-out single to put up another zero.

The Brewers were back on Rasmussen in the bottom of the fourth. With one out, Pratt drew a walk, and two pitches later, Sal Frelick lined a solid single into right, putting runners on the corners. David Hamilton, in a possible squeeze situation, eschewed the bunt and swung away, ultimately hitting what should've been a routine grounder to first. But Aranda, possibly with an eye on trying to get Pratt at home, booted it, and everyone was safe. The lead was down to one.

The Rays worked out of the inning, but after a Chourio groundout, Rasmussen walked Bauers, which ended his evening. He was replaced by the Rays' best lefty, Cam Booser, who faced Yelich; another manager may have gone to Andrew Vaughn as a pinch-hitter with the bases full and two out, but Pat Murphy rode with Yelich, who anticlimactically grounded out to second.

The Brewer pitcher in the fifth was Dustin May. With one out, Aranda lined a double into the right-field corner, but May was able to work out of it—Aranda moved to third on a Simpson groundout, but a Pratt made an assured play on a slow Caminero chopper to end the inning and strand the Ray first baseman at third.

Booser worked through the middle of the Brewers' order in the bottom of the fifth, allowing only a walk to Turang. DL Hall replaced May in the sixth and put himself in a hole when he hit the leadoff batter, Hicks, on the right forearm. He moved over on a sacrifice by Palacios, but Hall got the second out on a strikeout of Johnny DeLuca. Mesa Jr., though, came through with a two-out single to left, but Rays third base coach Brady Williams got extremely aggressive by sending his leadfooted catcher on a single to shallow left; Chourio's throw was on target, and Hicks was toast at home plate.

The Brewers seized the momentum from getting the final out at home. With lefty Ian Seymor on to face the bottom of the Brewer order, Frelick, of all people, battled for nine pitches, and on the last one he took a 93 mph fastball right over the heart of the plate and hit it out to center field. Tie ballgame.

Milwaukee kept making Seymour work hard. Hamilton fell into a 1-2 count but hit seven foul balls before striking out. Chourio saw eight pitches before he struck out. With two outs, Bauers worked a walk. Yelich, against another lefty, hit a pop-up to shallow left, but it was sort of in no-man's land between Walls, the shortstop, and Simpson, the left fielder. Some indecision about whose ball it was led to Simpson fielding it awkwardly; he had it in his glove, but he fell down while making the catch and when the glove hit the ground, the ball popped out. Bauers made it to third, while Yelich had a "single."

With runners on the corners and two out, the Rays needed to pull Seymour, who had thrown 34 pitches and not recored an out. Kevin Cash went to righty Tyler Wells to face Contreras, who was definitely the batter the Brewers wanted up in this situation. The move to Wells worked, though; Contreras grounded out to third to end the inning. Still, for the second time in three games, the Brewers had erased an early 4-0 deficit by the end of the sixth inning.

With the game tied, the Brewers pivoted firmly toward their "A" bullpen, as Abner Uribe entered the game in place of Hall, facing Walls and then, for the second time in two days, the top of the Tampa Bay order. Troublingly, Uribe walked Walls, the worst hitter on the Rays' roster, to set up the top of the order. Uribe got ahead of Díaz, and the Tampa Bay DH fouled off a bunch of pitches to stay alive, but Uribe finally got him with a slider for the first out. Aranda, who singled off of Uribe on Friday night, grounded out to second, but not until after Walls had stolen second base. With Walls at third and two out, Simpson was up, but he grounded out to first and Uribe's bad leadoff walk didn't come back on him.

With Wells still pitching, Turang got a rare at-bat against a right-handed reliever, and smoked the second pitch to the warning track in the right-field gap for a double. Mitchell also hit a ball deep to right but Mesa Jr. made a leaping catch in front of the wall; Turang was able to move to third, though, so it was a productive out. Cash went back to his bullpen and replaced Wells with another righty, Kevin Kelly, with Pratt at the plate.

Pratt delivered with the biggest hit of his young career. A base hit into right scored Turang from third, and the Brewers had flipped a 4-0 deficit into a 5-4 lead.

With Frelick back at the plate, Pratt stole second base, and the Brewers had another runner in scoring position with less than two outs. Frelick very nearly went yard again—he got into one, and the whole ballpark (and your humble scribe) thought he'd gotten his second of the game. But it held up on the warning track and Mesa Jr. made the catch for the second out. Hamilton grounded out, and Pratt was stranded, but not before he'd given the Brewers a late lead.

The Brewers now had a path to the end of the game in which they could avoid facing the top of the Rays order again. With the right-handed Caminero at the plate, Uribe stayed in the game with Aaron Ashby ready in the bullpen. Uribe got Caminero to chase a couple sliders that were way out of the zone, and on the fifth of five straight sliders from the Brewer righty, Caminero rolled over it harmlessly to shortstop for the first out. Ashby then replaced Uribe, and Cash countered by pinch-hitting Ryan Vilade for Hicks, and Ashby struck him out on a 3-2 changeup. Palacios hit a harmless grounder to second, which Turang flipped over to Bauers for the third out. Ashby was up to 14 2/3 scoreless innings this postseason.

With Kelly still pitching, Chourio led off the eighth with a single to center. Bauers flew out to the fringe of the warning track in left, but with Yelich up Chourio stole second base. Yelich drew a walk, and Contreras came to the plate to face Kelly, who was certainly on his last hitter. With Contreras at the plate, the Brewers executed a double steal, putting runners at second and third with one out. Contreras chased a 3-2 pitch and hit a grounder to shortstop, and Chourio was thrown out at home. The Brewers challenged, and it was very, very close, but for the second straight night, a very close, late-inning review on a run-scoring play went the Rays' way as the play stood. Kelly was replaced by lefty Steven Matz, and with two outs and runners on the corners, Turang battled and made decent contact but flew out down the left-field line to end the inning.

Ashby had only thrown nine pitches to get his two outs in the eighth, so the Brewers rolled him back out there with a one-run lead in the ninth, with the bottom of the order due up. But maybe the long bottom of the eighth was a detriment; DeLuca lined a double down the right-field line to start the inning, and the Rays let the Brewers know: it's not going to be that easy.

Trevor Megill warmed in the bullpen as Ashby faced Mesa Jr., but Ashby got back into the inning by striking him out on four pitches. The Rays sent pinch-hitter Ben Williamson to the plate in place of Walls, and he rolled a ball out to Turang. DeLuca advanced to third, but there were two out. Here's where Murphy had a choice to make: did he stick with Ashby, or did he bring on Megill to face the right-handed Yandy Díaz, who led the majors in batting average with runners in scoring position this year.

Murphy stuck with Ashby. Ashby fell behind 3-1. He worked it back full. On 3-2, Ashby put a curveball in the dirt. Díaz tried to check his swing, but first-base umpire James Hoye said he went around. It was close, but it was a just mirror of a non-call on Caminero's check swing in the ninth inning on Friday night. The game was over, and Ashby, by working out of trouble, added to his postseason legend.

This team's resiliency has been a trait all season, but now their ability to bounce back, their unwillingness to give in, their "never say die" attitude, has become their defining characteristic. Two games ago, the Brewers fell behind 4-0 to the Dodgers after Shohei Ohtani's three-run homer. It took them three innings to erase the deficit and a fourth to take the lead. Tonight, they fell behind 4-0, and it took them a whole six innings to erase the Rays' lead and seven to take the lead. How lazy of them.

The Brewers got offensive contributions up and down the roster; every batter in the lineup got at least one hit except for Hamilton, who reached on a run-scoring error and was credited with an RBI. In a postseason that keeps giving us new heroes, tonight it was Frelick, whose solo homer in the sixth tied the game, and Pratt, who atoned for his first-inning throwing error by knocking in the go-ahead, and ultimately winning, run in the seventh.

And then there was Ashby, this postseason's Grim Reaper. Tonight he was cruel enough to make Tampa Bay think they were going to get him before he buckled down and got the last three outs of the game. He's up to 15 2/3 scoreless innings in the postseason. No player has ever thrown that many innings and had a scoreless postseason; only Andrew Miller has a longer postseason streak, but if Ashby can get two more outs without allowing a run, he'll break that record, too.

Milwaukee now takes a 2-0 lead to Tampa. They say that seven-game postseason series don't really begin until someone wins a game on the road, but the Brewers have put themselves in excellent position by beating the Rays at what the Rays have done best all season: winning one-run games. After an off day tomorrow, we'll be back at it on Monday night at 7pm central time.

articles.title: ‘If we don’t…’ – What Lane Kiffin told LSU QB Sam Leavitt that led to dominant victory against Auburn
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin knew exactly what quarterback Sam Leavitt needed to do for the LSU Tigers to get their latest win, and he shared it after they beat Auburn. LSU f...
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin knew exactly what quarterback Sam Leavitt needed to do for the LSU Tigers to get their latest win, and he shared it after they beat Auburn.

LSU finally put together the kind of offensive performance Lane Kiffin has likely been looking for, beating Auburn 38-17. Sam Leavitt led the way with four total touchdowns and 387 passing yards, as the Tigers took a 31-10 lead into halftime and never looked back.

Wide receiver Jackson Harris had himself a game, finishing with 178 receiving yards and two touchdowns. It was a comfortable victory from the jump, and one that Lane Kiffin knew exactly what his quarterback had to do to achieve.

Lane Kiffin reveals his 'take care of the ball' advice to quarterback Sam Leavitt which led to the win

Turning the ball over has been one of Leavitt's biggest issues this season. He has already thrown eight interceptions this year, which has been a big problem for LSU. The team could have boasted an even better record than their current 6-2 showing.

Kiffin spoke after the game about how that needed to be addressed to secure the win against Auburn. He revealed exactly what he told his quarterback.

"I just told him that this was a game, you guys heard me say before, when I feel a game early that, 'OK, we're really going to dominate this game if we don't screw up,' I say that a lot to the players and to the quarterback especially," Kiffin said.

"'OK, hey, this is going to be a take-care-of-the-ball game,' because we're playing really well on the other side and we've got really good matchups. So he really played really well."

Leavitt had no turnovers against Auburn, which made a world of difference for the team. If he can continue to play like this, then Kiffin and the Tigers might just end up surprising some people this season.

articles.title: Why was former WWE and AEW wrestler Amber Nova arrested? Latest details emerge
articles.summary: The wrestling world has often seen superstars land in trouble with the law, and the latest name in that is former WWE NXT and AEW wrestler Amber Flora
articles.body: The wrestling world has often seen superstars land in trouble with the law, and the latest name in that is former WWE NXT and AEW wrestler Amber Flora (fka Amber Nova). The 34-year-old made waves during her tenures in both major companies. However, she recently made headlines, but for the wrong reasons, after being arrested by the police.Which charges led to the arrest of former WWE NXT and AEW wrestler Amber Nova? According to court documents filed in Orange County on October 24 and as reported by TMZ, Amber Nova was arrested on Friday, October 23, on DUI-related charges in Orlando, Florida, by an officer from the Orlando Police Department, Alvin Silverio. The arrest took place late at night at 1:48 AM near South Orange Blossom Trail and McLeod Road in Orlando.She was reportedly driving under the influence and refused to submit to DUI testing. The Orlando police put her behind bars, but she was released at 10:07 AM after depositing a bail amount of $2000.What are the latest details on Amber Nova’s arrest?The same court documents provided an in-depth look at the scene. Firstly, they indicated that there was no crash involved when Amber was arrested. After that, the 34-year-old wrestler was taken to the Orange County Sheriff’s Office DUI Testing Center. However, there were no valid samples collected, leaving the officials without a recorded blood alcohol concentration from the attempts they made.After the incident, Nova was summoned by the court, and she had to make a mandatory appearance on October 24. Furthermore, the next compliance date has been scheduled for November 2. As of now, there is no verdict on the authenticity of the allegations, and the case is not resolved, with the court process to be followed to do so. Moreover, the former AEW star is no longer in police custody.Amber Nova’s wrestling careerAmber Nova began her professional wrestling career in 2016 in Championship Wrestling Entertainment. After making significant waves, she made appearances in major promotions like Impact Wrestling, WWE NXT, and then AEW. As of now, she is a part of SHINE Wrestling. However, with Nova landing in hot water due to her legal trouble, it remains to be seen what the future holds for her.Also read: WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair hospitalized in Tampa following an accident outside Florida restaurantGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Virginia Tech Hokies Defeat Clemson in a Close Defensive Brawl: 20-16
articles.summary: Virginia Tech overcomes a 3rd quarter fade to come from behind to beat the Clemson Tigers 20-16. Luke Reynolds scores both Tech TDs and Ethan Grunkemeyer sho...
articles.body:
The Hokies had much going against them in this one, but the defense played as tough as Clemson's. The key being that final series for Clemson with the clock running out. We know the Hokies' bugaboos continue to plague them; dealing with running QBs, offensive line issues, and third quarter fades. This time though, Virginia Tech managed -4 stop after stop, and rallied up on offense to drive down the field and score in the air.

The Program called this the play of the game, and it was…

It was an Old Fashioned "Caveman Football" Effort

The Hokies once again defied the rules of probability and lost the coin toss. It's getting to be something that isn't really even worth it. The offense went much of nowhere, and the defense returned the favor for the Tigers. The score was knotted at 0-0 for three-quarters of the 1st period until Dabo decided to gamble on his side of the 50. Clemson went for it on 4th and short. Tech's defense had the range and the TFL to force the turnover on downs, but Tech's offense really didn't do a whole lot with the ball, either. That problem getting the ball across the goal line when in the red zone was an issue for both teams for this contest.

John Love was gold for the game, and his first field goal (37 yards) was also the first and last score of the first quarter. With the ice broken, Clemson found some success and drove the ball down into the Hokies' danger zone. The Tech defense managed a -4 stop as Clemson's very capable place kicker split the uprights from 34 yards out.

The Hokies tried a little "trickeration" on 4th down and they faked a punt, but the pattern was too far short of the sticks and Tech turned the ball over on downs inside their territory. The Hokie defense stepped up again, and not only stopped the Tigers, but managed to knock them out of field goal range. The ensuing Tech drive, presumably off the momentum of the stop, went all the way into the endzone for a nifty Ethan Grunkemeyer to Luke Reynolds touchdown.

Suddenly, close to the end of the half, the Hokies found themselves needing a stop and ahead 10-3. That doesn't sound great but given the tone and tempo of this game a touchdown lead was a serious hurtle to overcome for the Clemson offense.

After a convincing stop, and a Clemson punt the Hokies let the clock run out on the 3 or so seconds remaining before the half. Both teams went into their respective team rooms to go over what they thought worked and didn't. Hokie Nation worried because as we have seen all season, Tech has a "no good very bad thing" going with the third quarter.

If it wasn't something that you could just set a timer to, it's certainly something that some betting house is going to offer odds on whether or not Virginia Tech manages not to do it. The 3rd quarter heartburn was in serious need of some powerful antacids for this one. The first drive for Clemson, out of the break, set the Hokies back on their heels. Clemson's surprisingly good freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds managed to push pull prod, run, and pass in modest chunks to get the Tigers into field goal range before the Hokie defense finally caught and stopped them. The Tiger 49-yard field goal didn't put them ahead, but it did make the score a more manageable 10-6.

The Hokies, however, went 3 and out while going negative 9 yards on their next series. The OC either didn't make major adjustments to his game plan, or he figured that the Tigers weren't going to rush with overwhelming force. They did, and the slow developing plays that were called were just not up to defeating the very capable Clemson defensive line. Grunkemeyer was ultimately sacked 6 times in the game. Tech returned many of those favors on their QB, but neither offensive line was dominating the LOS.

Eventually Clemson drove the ball down the field as the Hokie defense sort of lost focus when the Tigers used the QB power to first get Tait Reynolds to move the ball 11 yards, and then repeat the same basic play to score after doing a very credible job getting passes off to his receivers. Reynolds scored the Tigers' only touchdown from 16 yards out. That put Clemson ahead by 3 points, 10-3, but it also woke up the Virginia Tech defense.

Tech's offense was still in a no-go zone, and the defense had to pull off a bend but don't break for a -4 with 3:48 left in the 3rd. The Hokies managed to return the favor on the ensuing kickoff, it was another -4 for Tech, but on the drive, they had managed to get the ball out faster, and Grunkemeyer's 27-yard strike to Que'Sean Brown might have proven something to Coaches Howle and Franklin. Quick passing plays were working under the zone and in the seams. That fact might have saved the Hokies as the game drew to a close.

A 16-13 game is not in the bag, unless the final whistle goes off. The problem was that Virginia Tech needed a touchdown to win, and a field goal to tie. There was a little birdie that told me Coach Franklin, known as a bit of a gambler, wasn't too interested in a tie and a trudge into overtime with the rules favoring no one since both offenses were struggling in the red zone.

Between the Love field goal at 12:00 on the 4th quarter clock, and the end of the game, the Hokies had to keep the Tigers from scoring anything. A field goal would make it difficult, and a touchdown would pretty much end the game. The Hokie defense managed a stop after 5 plays. Things started off pretty well with the Tigers eating up 18 quick yards, only to have the defensive line get enough pressure on Tait Reynolds that their 3rd and long attempt failed with a 3-yard loss. Que'Sean Brown put up a nice 15-yard return on the Clemson punt, but the Hokies had a holding penalty and two incomplete passes that made a nice 10-yarder to Q. Brown a big nothing. The Totten punt put the Tigers all the way back to their 7 yard line which forced the Tigers to try to run it out and they failed to get a 1st down.

The Hokies got the ball back with just short of 7 minutes on the clock. There were two issues there. First, the team needed that TD to win, but burn enough time off the clock, and get it close enough that in an emergency John Love's foot could tie it up without giving Clemson any chances.

Tech's final drive was interesting because Howle seemed to completely abandon the idea of a 4-minute offense, and went straight to what looked like a classic 2-minute drill. They were successful enough that Clemson's secondary began to get nervous and make mistakes. Both sides were probably pretty keyed up, because Tech made a few buffaloes too. They started off with a false start which put them five yards behind the sticks. Grunk had to scramble for 2 yards (it might have been a designed run, but at that point Tech wasn't running so it's safe to guess it was a scramble).

Then Grunkemeyer began to get some success. A quick shovel pass tunnel screen to Reynolds got 8, Grunk hit Fatrat Brown who got beyond the sticks and pulled off a pro sideline catch for the 1st down. That loosened up the defense a bit for Jeffery Overton to grab five yards and take a little time off the clock. Then Grunkemeyer hit Tyseer Denmark for first down. Then the strangest penalty play of the game came with a really ticky tack offensive holding call that was enforced, but Clemson's over-pumped secondary player shoved Grunkemeyer when Grunk was clearly out of bounds, which drew a 15-yard penalty and an automatic first down. The net for Tech was five yards.

Penalties doomed Clemson. A really obvious PI was called that gave the Hokies another 1st down and put the ball on the Clemson 29. They did it again, on 2nd down and 10 and that foul put the ball on Clemson's 14 with a brand-new set of downs. Tech would have trouble with calls at the line and get called for a false start on Grunkemeyer. Grunk got most of the penalty yards back on the next play, with his legs, and then got Q. involved again to get a solid 10-yard play down to the Tiger 5-yard line. It wasn't a 1st down though.

Nail biting time… The Hokies tried a pass in the corner of the endzone to Ja'Ricous Hairston, but it just didn't work on the timing and placement. That was a 3rd and 1 play. Okay, now someone get Coach Franklin a Riverboat Gambler hat… The game was on the line; John Love would have tied it up with no problems from the snap at the 5. Grunk and the line set up to be a tush push QB sneak. But Benji Gosnell went in motion, drawing coverage and confusing the zone coverage in the secondary. Grunkemeyer backpedaled and flipped a flat-footed soft toss to a wide-open Luke Reynolds who had taken advantage of the busted coverage.

Total time and effort for the drive? 4:48 minutes on 11 plays covering 69 yards. What was left on the clock was 1:41 when Clemson set up on the 25-yard line.

The big joke circulating on the chats was along the lines of "Brrrring!!! Brent, this is Bud… BLITZ!!!!" Though it's not a joke… In prior efforts at the end of the game, Brent Pry has put Prevent Defenses on the field to try to slow down the offense and burn off clock, and it's rarely worked (and it rarely does). We saw some of it to start the first few plays of the final series. Clemson chopped off 32 yards to their 48. At that point, commenters were about to throw in the towel. There was 1:22 left on the clock, and the entire defensive posture changed on a dime. Jaquez White came knifing in from his cornerback position and sacked Tait Reynolds for 7 yards. Reynolds would get the yardage back but not the down with a completed pass on the next play. On 3rd down and 9 yards to go, heavy pressure and solid coverage cause an incomplete pass and set up a 4th and 9. Folks this was nail biting time. It was the game. And we saw, above, Mylachi Williams pull off big inside big rush, supported by another Jaquez White blitz that pinched in Tait Reynolds and dropped him in the backfield to force a turnover on downs. That ended the game.

All Tech had to do, was kneel it out for two plays.

Thing #1: The Virginia Tech Hokies have defeated Dabo Swinney's Clemson Tigers for the first time since the Beamer Era. The win puts Tech at 6-2, with a 3-2 ACC record. Let's not get ahead of ourselves, but this team has proven to itself, and its opponents that it is for real, and a serious threat every time it takes the field. No more doubts, now.

Thing #2: The Virginia Tech Hokies are now bowl eligible . This team finally has a chance to cross the .500 mark for a season, and it no longer has to sweat down to the final game to see if there will be a post season. My guess is that any opponents are likely to face an intact team for a bowl, too.

Thing #3: The Hoos lost again. That's always a good reason to celebrate.

Sometimes Byes can be good, and sometimes they can let the rust creep in. Let's see how Coach Franklin and staff deal with this 2-week break. There will be some time to get some players rested up and back on available status. November 6th, the Hokies show up in Dallas, Texas to play SMU. The Mustangs aren't as daunting as they looked at the beginning of the season, but Tech has its work cut out for it.

It's also the final four games, and the last 3rd of the season. The Final Risk Chart is due out. Remember the floor was 7-5 or 8-4 ( if the Hokies beat Pitt or Clemson ). Well, they finished the 2nd 3rd 2-2 and beat Clemson. We'll see how it goes from here. Both SMU and Miami were just put on notice.

articles.title: Dmitri Simashev scores his second goal in OT as Mammoth beat Lightning 5-4
articles.summary: SALT LAKE CITY (AP) — Dmitri Simashev scored his second goal of the game at 1:44 of overtime as the Utah Mammoth beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 5-4 on Saturday...
articles.body:
SALT LAKE CITY (AP) — Dmitri Simashev scored his second goal of the game at 1:44 of overtime as the Utah Mammoth beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 5-4 on Saturday night.

Simashev's first goal tied the game at 4-4 with 2:28 remaining in the second period.

Nikita Kucherov became Tampa Bay's franchise leader in points when he assisted on Brayden Point's goal with 7:18 remaining in the first period. That put him at 1,138 career points, one more than former teammate Steven Stamkos, who had held the record since April 2022.

Kucherov has played his entire career with Tampa Bay, starting in 2013.

Kailer Yamamoto, Dylan Guenther and Anders Lee also scored for the Mammoth. Vincent Trocheck had two assists, while Clayton Keller, Andrew Peeke, Mackenzie Weegar and Sergachev each recorded one assist.

Charle-Edouard D'Astous, Pontus Holmberg and Conor Geekie had the other goals for the Lightning. D'Astous, Ryan McDonagh, Scott Sabourin and Erik Cernak had assists.

Tampa Bay took a 1-0 lead with 14:50 remaining in the first period. D'Astous was credited with a goal after a Mammoth player tried to tap the puck to goalie Karel Vejmelka, but it went between his legs and into the net.

Yamamoto evened the score with a breakaway goal less than two minutes later. Holmberg scored with 9:54 remaining for a 2-1 advantage.

Point put the Lightning up 3-1 with 7:18 remaining in the opening period. Guenther cut the deficit to 3-2 on a power play with 2:21 left in the first.

Geekie gave Tampa Bay a 4-2 lead with 14:28 remaining in the second period. Lee answered with 5:21 remaining.

articles.title: Cardinals vs. Broncos opponent preview and predictions
articles.summary: Broncos Wire writer Brandon Walker takes Cardinals fans behind enemy lines, giving them a look at the Broncos.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals will face the Denver Broncos on Sunday at State Farm Stadium. It is the first time since 2022 they have faced the Broncos and it is only the 13th time ever in the regular season.

The Cardinals are coming off a big win over the Los Angeles Rams , beating them 18-16 on a last-second field goal. The Broncos beat the Seattle Seahawks last Thursday 17-14 in overtime.

Before the two teams play, Broncos Wire contributing writer Brandon Walker gives Cardinals some insight as he answered questions I had about the Broncos and the matchup.

What is going well and not so well offensively for the Broncos? Is Bo Nix still the guy?

I may be in the minority of people who still think Bo Nix has what it takes as a starter for the Denver Broncos. Yes, things have been difficult in the early going, but the Broncos have faced some really stout defenses, and have not turned the ball over. Despite Nix's numbers, the Broncos have been taking care of the football. I would say the hardest thing to do right now is trying to complete a deep shot, something which should be possible with the Broncos' speedy receiving corps.

It feels like the defense has played unevenly this season. What is going well and not so well there?

After laying an absolute egg in Week 1, the Broncos defense has settled into its own, with the key difference from last year to this year being forcing turnovers. Denver turned over the Los Angeles Rams several times, and forced three turnovers in Week 6. At times, the Broncos have struggled with finishing tackles, but they are coming into their element as we enter the second third of the season.

Are you expecting any midseason changes like a trade?

As much as fans here would love to see the Broncos trade for a player like Colts running back Jonathon Taylor to help jumpstart a very anemic running game, I simply don't see the Broncos making a move at the deadline. Denver has the players they believe can make a difference and bring them deep into the latter half of the year.

Which matchups most favor the Broncos? Which ones favor the Broncos?

I believe Denver's pass rushers are going to be the great equalizer in Week 7. The Broncos have the option to bring back edge rusher Jonathon Cooper after a six-month stint on the commissioner's exempt list for offseason troubles, and adds speed and a better run game presence than those who replaced him through six weeks.

The Cardinals, if they are able to stop the run, will make the Broncos' offense one-dimensional. Teams have virtually dared Denver to throw the ball on them, and I think that Week 7 will be more of the same.

I think this may be the game the Broncos' offense finally breaks out. If that is the case, Nix can quiet some of his harshest critics (aka Ryan Fitzpatrick) with a big game. Arizona has played well, including coming off a huge win against the Rams in LA. That being said, I think Denver may pull away in the 4th quarter, in a 28-18 win. Broncos 28, Cardinals 18

Get more Cardinals and NFL coverage from Cards Wire's Jess Root and others by listening to the latest on the Rise Up, See Red podcast. Subscribe on Spotify , YouTube or Apple Podcasts .

articles.title: Detroit Red Wings play with fire, scorched by Flames in 2nd period
articles.summary: Detroit Red Wings score: Andrew Copp tied it at 1 in the second period before three straight goals by the Calgary Flames on Saturday, Oct. 24.
articles.body:
A couple nights after facing hardly any shots, Detroit Red Wings goalie John Gibson saw far too many in a rough second period against the Calgary Flames on Saturday, Oct. 24.

Gibson surrendered three goals on 10 shots in the second, breaking a tie as the Wings fell to the Flames, 4-1, at Scotiabank Saddledome to snap a six-game point streak for Detroit (4-4-3).

It was a strong contrast from his two periods of work on Thursday in Vancouver, when he faced just five shots – stopping four – in a 5-2 win over the Canucks.

See Detroit Red Wings make final visit to Saddledome vs Calgary Flames

The loss was the Wings' final game at the Saddledome, which will be replaced with a new arena for the 2027-28 arena. The Wings finished their run at the Saddledome, which opened for the 1983-84 season, with a 30-33-2-2 regular-season record at the arena shaped like, well, a saddle.

The loss also kept the Wings from fully joining an increasingly crowded Eastern Conference wild-card picture: at 11 points, the Wings are one point back of a block of four teams (Washington Capitals, New York Islanders, Montreal Canadiens and Florida Panthers) tied for the second and final wild-card spot.

After going into the second period trailing 1-0 on a Joel Farabee goal, the Wings evened it on a two-man hustle play from J.T. Compher and Andrew Copp, 2:22 in. Copp sent the draw from the left side dot toward the net, where Compher chased it down and tried to put a shot on net. Goalie Devin Cooley stopped that one, but Copp, trailing to the far right post, tapped it past Cooley for his second goal of the season, and his first since Oct. 15.

The tie lasted a little over six minutes before former Saginaw Spirit star Zayne Parekh scored a wrister on the power play for his first goal this season, and sixth of his career. About 9½ minutes later, Ryan Strome stretched it to a two-goal lead with a snap shot past Gibson. That was followed less than 90 seconds later by a snapper past Gibson on the power play by Matvei Gridin.

The Red Wings will wrap up their four-game Western Conference road swing with a stop in Edmonton on Monday (9:30 p.m., Detroit SportsNet). The Oilers (8-2-1) enter Sunday tied for first in the Pacific Division, but they won't be resting on their laurels after a rough game Saturday night – a 7-2 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs. Former MVP Leon Draisaitl scored both goals for the Oilers, assisted both times by Connor McDavid. The Oilers captain is on a monster tear to open the season, as his pair of helpers brought him to an NHL-best 33 points – eight goals, 25 assists – in just 11 games; that's an 84-game pace of 252 points, which would be 38 more than the NHL record of 215 set by Wayne Gretzky in 1985-86 (albeit in only an 82-game season).

The Wings return to their non-saddle-shaped arena on Thursday as they host the Chicago Blackhawks , followed by a Halloween afternoon date with the St. Louis Blues.
